title: Section A — Integration and limits — Q1
body:
Evaluate \(\int_0^1 3x^2 e^{x^3}\,dx\). Show the substitution explicitly.
Student work: Let \(u = x^3\), so \(du = 3x^2\,dx\); the bounds transform as \(u : 0 \to 1\), giving \(\int_0^1 e^u\,du = e - 1\).
criteria: 4 pts for the substitution \(u = x^3\), 4 pts for transformed bounds \(u : 0 \to 1\), 2 pts for the value \(e - 1\)

title: Section A — Integration and limits — Q2
body:
Compute \(\lim_{n \to \infty} \left(1 + \frac{2}{n}\right)^{n}\).
Student work: Write \(\left(1 + \frac{2}{n}\right)^{n} = e^{n \ln(1 + 2/n)}\); since \(n \ln(1 + 2/n) \to 2\), the limit is \(e^2\).
criteria: 6 pts for reducing to an exponential limit (e.g. \(e^{n \ln(1 + 2/n)}\)), 4 pts for the value \(e^2\)

title: Section B — Series convergence — Q3
body:
Determine whether \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{n!}{n^n}\) converges. Justify with a named test.
Student work: Ratio test — \(\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} = \left(\frac{n}{n+1}\right)^{n} \to \frac{1}{e} < 1\), hence the series converges.
criteria: 5 pts for a correct ratio-test setup, 5 pts for the limit \(1/e < 1\) and the conclusion

title: Section B — Series convergence — Q4
body:
Prove that \(\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n \ln^2 n}\) converges.
Student work: The terms are smaller than \(\frac{1}{n^2}\), so it converges by comparison with \(\sum \frac{1}{n^2}\).
criteria: 6 pts for the integral test or Cauchy condensation with hypotheses checked, 4 pts for a correct evaluation; a bare comparison with \(\sum 1/n^2\) is invalid and earns at most 2 pts
